_doc: Generator knobs. Every knob is a [easy, hard] pair interpolated by the search's pressure p in [0, 1], then jittered by the mutation step. Costs are in currency at costScale 1 unless keyed salvage.*.

rings._doc: Half extents of the perimeter ring around the core (world units), and sections per side (top/bottom, left/right).

traderRoute._doc: Grid cell, clearance from footprints and walls, and half the gate door opening (world units).

lots._doc: Lots and streets (POLISH-PLAN item 7B): streets of street units cross at the core (its plaza) and repeat every block + street; square lots of block units between them; buildings keep to one lot along each axis they fit.

defendWaves._doc: Swarmlings per wave = swarm knob x share: wave 0 firstShare, then +earlyGrowth per wave; weak raids each come from one attack side; from wave lateFrom on (levels with towers or guards to buy) +lateGrowth per wave, packed at lateGap seconds apart instead of gap, from every attack side. Raiders = swarm x (late)Raiders x wave index. The early raids grow until they drop dropsPerEarlyNeed x the walls and one tower per attack side; then the packed waves grow together until all but the last drop dropsPerNeed x the core of the purchase ladder (walls, the first guards, med bay, and a tower and its Lv2 on every socket standing from the start: Batch 3 sizes the waves against it; Lv3s and later sockets are left to build to the end); each packed wave stays lateStep x the wave before it. With towers or guards to buy there are at least lateFrom + 2 waves. On med bay levels a probe raid (raid) comes through a breach in a quiet side at t s, before the player has scrap to wall it. A defend survive goal lasts surviveTail s past the start of the wave before the last.

defendSockets._doc: Batch 3 turret sockets at each attack gate. Spots are [u, v] in world units in the gate's frame: u along the wall from the gate's middle, v outward (negative = inside). start sockets per gate stand from the start, taking inside and outside spots in turn; each unlock opens n more (outside spots first when outside is true) at the gate the next wave comes to, once that many waves have started (capped at the last wave). A spot with no room tries its mirror across the wall, then gives up; a gate with fewer than start sockets fails the layout. A site keeps edge from the map edge, wallClear from every wall, laneClear from the attack lane (the straight line out from the gate) and siteR from every station centre; search is how far it may drift from the wanted spot. An outside socket's pad stands padIn inside the wall. Gatherables (forest nodes) on a socket's spot give way.

terrain._doc: Geography (R3 item 17). chance = share of levels per family that get terrain; pieces = [min, max]; sizes in world units; gaps are clearances to stations, the core, walls, the map edge and the straight lines residents walk.

search._loop: REDESIGN-R3 item 7: reject when the reference bot repeats one player trip (same source type, resource, target; trips a worker already performs are not counted) more than loopCap times in a row. Each reject raises an ease level by 1/loopEaseSteps: hire prices drop up to loopHireCut, core burn slows by up to loopBurnEase, level length shrinks by up to loopLengthCut, start currency grows by up to loopStartCurrency.

humanStars._doc: BACKLOG-R4 Batch 2: stars are earned by the human-view bot (bots HUMAN profile: human reaction, a little error, sees only the screen and the HUD), not the omniscient good bot. Each star objective (challenges and the time target) must be earned on at least minEarned of `seeds` in-level seeds, and at least one seed must take all three stars. 4 of 6 (two thirds) is a star a careful player earns on most attempts without luck or off-screen knowledge; one seed in three may miss it, which keeps the star a challenge. The good bot's old bar was 1 three-star seed in 10. levels:check replays the same seeds and fails a level whose human stars fall more than regressTolerance below the mean recorded at generation (rating.stars.human).
